comparison.basis: Identity presence in two differently scoped snapshots; no creation, acceptance, send or progression event is inferred.

warnings: Retain the complete October 16 deal/activity snapshot as the dated baseline. This supplement does not replace its all-status records, source fields or activity history.
Pipeline stage totals are open-view source inventories across everyone; they include any tests or duplicate companies. Do not sum them into a cleaned account-wide business total.
Visible cards are a bounded, virtualized browser subset. Truncated URLs stay unresolved; no hidden record IDs were reconstructed.
A latest-update label is not a call, Video DM send, accepted opportunity or stage-transition event. Source label timezone was not exposed.
Closed Won and Closed Lost are stage labels. Actual status, won/lost timestamps and first-client evidence must establish business outcomes.
Stage header monetary labels differ from visible card values in Sales. Weighting/amount basis is unverified; neither is revenue or verified qualified pipeline.
NuVee deal788 remains qualified/warm by explicit owner confirmation despite its current Parking Lot (Short Term) position. No acceptance date or active commercial next step has been confirmed.

Venus appears under two deal IDs (791 in Leads and805 in Sales). The owner-confirmed unqualified lead disposition is not automatically reversed by the other record stage. Reconcile company identity and owner disposition.
The source export could not be completed through the available Chrome download interaction. A refreshed all-status deal export, activity export and event/stage history remain needed.

incrementalReview.scope: Default non-deleted all-accessible-owner deal updates; separately deleted deals; all accessible activities; recents for deal/activity/person/organization/note; separately all accessible archived deals. Each source has its own captured collection time.
incrementalReview.result: No changes returned in overlapping accessible deal/update queries, and all924 currently returned activity records exactly match the retained state. The original full inventory timestamp is unchanged; the separately dated state bridge supports complete October23 state reporting plus partial October24 observation, within the accessible source scope.

effectiveCoverage.sourceBasis: Overlapping updated-since reads for accessible non-deleted and deleted deals, accessible activity updates and recent changes from before the earliest baseline request; separately all accessible archived deals; fresh fully paginated done/undone activity census with user_id0 compared by unique ID and every returned field against all924 retained activity records. All changes/ID removals/additions were zero. The source checks are non-atomic. This verifies retained accessible state, not all historical deleted events, source writes or commercial outcomes.

records.messageDateBasis: Displayed source message date and retained 2026 thread context; no exact source instant or message timezone was established.

notes: Eight thread records are a targeted context sample, not eight meetings, new prospects, accepted opportunities or sends.
The Venus reschedule and replacement invitation describe one booking chain; accepted future Quantex/Jumbo invitations do not establish held calls.
Thirteen accessible UI searches were inspected. Zero keyword results are bounded search findings, not proof of account-wide absence; alternate company/contact queries can find relevant threads.
NuVee search results were inspected without opening either thread. Its existing owner-confirmed qualified status and held-call decision remain unchanged.
Source message dates, scheduled event dates and source collection times are distinct. Date-only message observations keep unknown source timezone and no invented UTC timestamp.
No source records or messages were edited or sent. CRM state checks, all event counters, owner decisions, commercial outcomes and human-hour estimates are unchanged.
Raw messages, addresses, subjects, meeting access details and unrelated private context remain outside the public supplement.

sourceCoverage.collectionMethod: Read-only connector, every bounded main/accepted tab range with before/after file modification clock.
sourceCoverage.inventoryGrain: Contact/prospect rows plus a separately retained company-only target cohort.
sourceCoverage.excludedNonProspectPhysicalRowsBasis: Returned body rows with no named organization target:4281 have no static input values and one row135 contains only a rank value. The50 named company-only targets are retained separately, not excluded as blank/non-target rows.
sourceCoverage.contactRowEligibility: Nonempty organization and contact, excluding header rows. This is contact-row grain, not the entire workbook target inventory.
sourceCoverage.companyOnlyTargetEligibility: Nonempty organization and empty contact; all50 observed rows have a literal ICP score, QC Pending - Not Activated status and Review action. No contact or commercial qualification is inferred.
sourceCoverage.completeWithinWorkbookMeaning: All returned named organization target rows are represented at their disclosed contact-row or company-only grain. The full allocated main/accepted ranges were read; this does not establish complete account-wide outreach or qualified pipeline.
sourceCoverage.sourceAppearanceCohort: Existing first-appearance revision comparisons cover the retained contact-row identity cohort, using profiles where available and company/contact fallback identities otherwise. The50 company-only rows are outside that cohort; its existing52/147distinct floors and52/152row-occurrence floors are unchanged.

connectionDiagnostics.helperRuleBasis: Current connection date values were cross-checked against accepted-profile attributes. Formula definitions retain their earlier separately dated review.

notes: November 19 full worksheet values and date fields were collected with a stable Drive file clock across the read.
Literal date fields retain their source calendar day. Exact event timestamps and upstream synchronization times are unavailable.
Current status, recording assets and worksheet response labels describe source records. Native conversation observations retain their original collection dates.
Revision comparisons establish lower bounds for first appearances. Forty-seven current rows cross the November 18/19 Mountain cutoff and remain unassigned to either reporting day.
The retained CRM reconciliation covers its fixed October 30–November 12 cohort. Current row and asset continuity was checked; CRM source observations retain their original clocks.

missingDealReview.status: Existing fresh CRM review independently confirms deleted.
missingDealReview.action: Retain stale Sheet ID as a quality issue; do not silently remap.

crmJoin.attributionRule: Automation defaults to Christian. Explicit workflow/sender evidence and identity joins are required; CRM owner alone does not establish Charles outreach.

limits: Revision date and author are file-level metadata, not actual send time or cell-level authorship.
DMd is a self-reported message status; video inclusion and delivery are unverified.
Other Note research/tier labels do not establish Charles-qualified companies.
Google date serials and TRUE casing were normalized before comparison, removing109 spurious field differences.

sourceVerification.note: Source metadata, revision history and stable joins were reviewed independently; no later worksheet value change was established. File-level status entry dates do not establish actual send time, channel or video inclusion.

historyReview.note: All 85 retained pages were reviewed:841 displayed entries represent808 distinct IDs. The 33 repeated IDs occur across adjacent pages with identical status/time. Tied, non-atomic pagination can repeat or omit items; these are retained observations, not a certified complete execution census. The703 held IDs are technical history, not an evidenced business-data deficit.

reconciliation.sampleSelection: Targeted sample spread through retained history, not a random or complete eligibility audit.
reconciliation.note: 703 distinct held IDs cluster into one approximately two-second Google Sheets trigger burst. Four reviewed payloads contain only row identifiers/hash data; two contain prospect data with blank Sent and Loom fields. None of these six establishes an eligible sent-video CRM write. This is consistent with bulk-trigger flood protection; the exact initiating edit and all-row eligibility remain unverified.

automationReview.note: Existing logged-in Zapier session used; no Google account selection or new sign-in was needed. The pre-existing draft was neither edited nor published.
limits: No held entries were replayed and no workflow configuration was changed.
ColumnQ is Loom Link; columnP is the downstream Status filter. Different source fields alone do not establish a mapping defect.
The verified October 21 ten-record Loom cohort is present in CRM. The703 held IDs do not establish703 intended syncs, missed messages or missing records.
Waalaxy upstream synchronization and actual LinkedIn sender, sending time and delivery remain separate evidence gaps.

metadataFreshnessCheck.valuesFreshnessLabel: Values collected October 21 at 19:02 Mountain; unchanged source reverified October 22 at 06:11 Mountain.
provenanceLimits: Drive modification/revision checks establish unchanged file state, not the freshness or completeness of an upstream Waalaxy synchronization.
Upstream sender account, exact sending timestamps and delivery remain unverified.
No browser, wrong-account collection, source writes, shared edits or publication performed.

explicitReplyReports.basis: The CRM note explicitly reports an April 29 reply. This is not a platform message receipt and does not establish video attribution, qualification, a held call or a new commercial outcome.

notes: Existing worksheet Send status dates are exposed as reported dates; these are not additional sends.
The ten October 21 video-asset CRM matches establish source provenance. Their note timestamps reflect synchronization; native message corroboration, when available, is recorded separately.
Retained Waalaxy first/latest LinkedIn dates are person attributes with date-only precision. Actual sender identity and video inclusion are unverified.
One CRM note explicitly reports an April 29 reply. Its May 1 note creation date is not the reply date; commercial outcome classifications are unchanged.
Associated mail evidence is historical email, kept separate from Video DM reporting. The unsent draft is excluded.
CRM task due/completion timestamps and planned sequence dates are not actual sends. No replay, outreach or source record changes were performed.

Native Charles LinkedIn conversations were checked for all ten October 21 Loom-linked profiles. Nine exact outbound Loom assets are visible on Wednesday, corroborating the October 21 worksheet date. These are existing reported sends now corroborated by platform evidence, not nine additional sends to add to the worksheet count.

SubImage remains source-reported Sent but platform send unconfirmed: the visible Charles conversation ends in February text outreach and does not expose the referenced October Loom asset. This does not establish that no send occurred.
No inbound reply after the nine matching videos was visible in this bounded review. There is no account-wide verified reply count or zero, and seen indicators are not replies or video views.

Cypher’s incoming message displays Monday (October 19 when anchored to this October 22 observation), while its Waalaxy latest-reply attribute says October 20. Both source dates are preserved without assuming timezone conversion. No visible video attribution or commercial outcome is established.

Native observations expose weekday labels and local display times, not source timezones or stable message/conversation IDs. Day precision is retained and occurredAt remains null; no midnight UTC timestamp is fabricated.

The older Waalaxy latest-message attributes for several matched profiles precede actual October 21 platform video messages. They are retained as source attributes and should not be used as complete or current message history.

Current worksheet inventory/date reports were refreshed independently. Every native observation retains its original observedAt, displayed day, precision and historical row; newer inventory collection does not re-date native proof.

Fresh October 22 video-asset checks corroborate existing worksheet reports; they are not added again to reported-send totals. Unchecked profiles remain pending, not verified zero or unconfirmed sends.

October 24 targeted checks add three historical September video sends and one attributed September declined reply. October verified video sends remain 18; source literal date/status reports are unchanged. Navigara/Dark Watch latest October messages are general text, and Sonata is a video reference with an unverified short-link destination.

October 28/29 native refresh adds only explicitly selected authored/date/time blocks. Follow-up texts are separate events, source worksheet follow-up dates remain separate reports, and prior message proof retains its original clocks.
Four exact recipient threads add three historical video sends, one explicit video follow-up and four historical inbound replies. Only Sid explicitly acknowledges the video and follow-up.

Rob states that he already has a CFO; Jared directs Charles to a colleague; Razvan supplies a meeting-platform route. These general replies do not establish video attribution, qualification, actual introductions, confirmed bookings or held calls.
Jared’s literal worksheet No Response status is retained alongside the independently dated October7 inbound reply.

The already observed Razvan October28 video retains its original observation fields and clock. The new native check is appended only as repeat provenance; current source company and displayed native asset title both identify Pilot Protocol.
Undated Seen markers on later reminder or meeting exchanges are excluded from these video and reply events. No video views are inferred.
All additions retain their September/October source days. November12–18 and November1–18 selected activity remain unchanged; account-wide coverage is incomplete.

posts.title: Thank you, Devo Harris, for trusting Centripetal Advisors with Adventr's needs and sharing your experience working with us in this testimonial video  🙏

Is the Rule of 40 still relevant for SaaS #founders?

While companies that achieve it often command premium exit multiples (10.5x vs. ~6x EV/Revenue), the reality is that most public SaaS businesses fall well short of this benchmark. 

In this post, we explore:

✅  What the Rule of 40 is and represents
✅  How many companies actually meet the threshold
✅  Whether it remains a meaningful metric in today’s market

We also examine how founders should think about the Rule of 40 based on stage -- and when it’s most strategic to use it as a performance signal versus a guiding principle.

📌 Additional resources for founders are included at the end 📌 

#RuleOf40 #SaaSFounders #StartupMetrics #CapitalEfficiency #Fundraising #VCReadiness #B2BStartups #FounderInsights #B2BSaaS #FractionalCFO #CentripetalAdvisors

In this video, Megadata Health Systems CEO Shalom Reinman shares his experience partnering with the Centripetal Advisors team. 

Together, we:
 ✅ Raised $12.5M in debt and equity with top-tier backers (TIMIA Capital, Avidbank, Blueprint Equity, Channel Equity Partners, Blossom Street Ventures )
 ✅ Built a SaaS-native financial infrastructure, board reporting, and KPI frameworks
 ✅ Offloaded financial operations from the founder—freeing him to focus on growth
✅ Took a board seat and invested directly in the company

💡 Founders: if its unclear how your finance function is actually helping you scale, watch the video to hear how the right partner can make all the difference. 

#FractionalCFO #CapitalRaising #StartupFinance #SaaSFounders #B2BStartups #VentureDebt #SeriesA #StrategicFinance #CentripetalAdvisors
From our founder, Charles Solomon. When it comes to fundraising (in the immortal words of Montell Jordan) This Is How We Do It!
🚀  $16M Closed in Q1. Zero Term Sheets to Done Deals in 54 Days. 👏

From our conversations with LP-backed Series A investors and funds still deploying, the message is crystal clear: 

in 2025, capital flows will bifurcate.

Some of it will chase AI-driven breakout potential....

The rest? 
It’s going to highly disciplined, well-prepared companies that know their numbers cold—not just those with a good story.

❗The middle—companies that are “fine but fuzzy”—will be ignored.

Here’s what we’re seeing:

-⏱️ Deal cycles are getting longer.
-🔍 Diligence standards are higher.
-📉 Valuations are softening—unless you're in the top decile of metrics.
-💡 Operational discipline = capital optionality.
-🧩 M&A is back on the table as a way to grow smarter in a tighter market.
--------------------------------------------
So what does this mean for founders? You must know:

- How do you benchmark against your peers?
- Can you tell the capital story that fits your stage, risk profile, and growth ambitions?
- Is your strategy built for this market—or the one you wish you were in?

If you don’t have sharp answers, you need sharper partners.

At Centripetal Advisors, we help B2B founders build the financial strategy, investor materials, and operating discipline needed to command capital—debt or equity. And in a world where mediocrity is being re-priced, that edge is everything.

Let’s talk about your capital strategy:

posts.title: Remember Marcus from the Magic Number series? He's back. Poor Marcus still never closed a deal, but every dollar the company paid him belongs in CAC.

Marcus is back from the Magic Number series, and he still never closed a deal. This article covers reported vs. pro forma CAC, why the two pro formas aren't cumulative, how to handle numbers too small to trust, and the checklist behind the whole week.
The same fictional company has a CAC of $34K, $102K, $132K and $593K, and none of those numbers is wrong.

The same company can show a CAC of $34K or $593K without a single error. The difference is the window you divide by. This article covers lagging spend to your sales cycle, why short windows break on small numbers, and why we're not fans of splitting sales and marketing timing at Seed through Series B.

Most CAC calculations I see are missing somebody's salary.

Most CAC calculations are missing somebody's salary: payroll taxes coded to G&A, the founder's selling time, the solutions engineer on every demo. This article covers what fully loaded means, how to allocate anyone with real GTM time, and what all-in CAC carries when expansion is big.

Ideally, companies would use the same process to calculate CAC (a process that involves at least understanding your sales cycle, so get ready for that). In practice, just like the Magic Number, the calculation is more complicated than the surface formula.

CAC looks like simple math: sales and marketing spend divided by the new customers you won. Underneath it are four decisions, and each one moves the number on its own. This article walks through the formula, a worked example on the same fictional company from our Magic Number series, and the difference between blended and paid CAC.

notes: Fresh read uses the configured Centripetal Fireflies MCP; no browser terms acceptance or sign-in was needed.

Historical metadata collection (2026-10-21 Mountain): One hundred metadata records cross October 1; 76 are indexed in October. This is complete indexed-October coverage within the accessible list, not complete actual-meeting or attendance coverage.

The minimized detailed register combines earlier retained reviews with fresh dialogue reviews; it is not the entire metadata list and overlapping recording segments are not automatically unique meetings.
Nicolette October 12 and DEXIQ October 2 have actual Charles dialogue and independently corroborated occurrence days. Exact meeting-start and individual attendance times remain unknown.
The eleven October 19–21 recordings establish no additional Charles prospect calls. This bounded absence is not an account-wide zero.
Conditional internal discussion of future XCaliber/Venus engagements does not establish signed client wins.

Thirteen additional selected October-indexed dialogues were read independently: twelve establish recruiting, vendor, referral or existing-client purposes; one has insufficient dialogue. None adds a confirmed prospect outcome. Metadata/index times remain distinct from actual meeting occurrence; complete held-call coverage is still unresolved.

Historical purpose review (2026-10-22 Mountain): 76 successful responses: 65 purposes classified, five insufficient dialogues and six responses with no dialogue. Nine metadata duplicate-candidate groups are retained separately from a previously verified audio duplicate. No additional eligible prospect call or dated first-client win was established. Complete actual call coverage remains unknown.

The October 23 refresh scans 100 current metadata records including 84 October IDs; eight new dialogues and 11 prior empty/fragmentary responses were reviewed. Prior commercial decisions remain unchanged.
The October 22 longer GTM audio is 96.19 minutes and has Christian email plus speaker attribution. A parallel 30-minute transcript overlaps it and is not another meeting.

Latest metadata collection scans 150 records across October 1 and retains 97 October-indexed IDs. Thirteen new bodies and eleven prior insufficient responses were reviewed. Older body evidence keeps its original collection age; no new owner commercial decisions are applied.

The new Fireflies metadata pages span before October 1 and retain November activity. Collection, transcript indexing, independent occurrence dates and manual commercial decisions have distinct evidence clocks.
